input:
The IT provider corpITOp requires a service to manage 5,000 office employees. This service must filter dangerous websites, 
scan downloaded files for malware, and ensure that sensitive data does not leave the network. Regarding requirements, 
ensuring a mandatory latency below 10 milliseconds, the service chain establishes a connection between a webFilterVF allocated at the edge 
and a malwareScannerVF located in the cloud. Following this, guaranteeing a bandwidth greater than 500 mbps, the service proceeds to connect 
the malwareScannerVF to a dlpEngineVF located in the cloud.

The media provider cinemaRenderOp requires a service to manage 5,000 rendering projects. This infrastructure receives raw digital scenes, 
distributes the rendering computation across hundreds of virtual nodes, and reassembles the finished frames for post-production. Preferring 
that the total chain hardware is lower than 800 gb. Specifying that compression is applied after the initial function, the service 
begins with a sceneReceiverVF allocated at the edge connected to an assetValidatorVF located in the cloud, a renderDistributorVF located in the 
cloud, and a frameAssemblerVF located in the cloud. Ensuring that caching is executed before the final node, the system completes 
the pipeline with a colorGraderVF located in the cloud.

The media provider liveSubsOp requires a live subtitling service to manage 10,000 concurrent streams. This service intercepts the audio 
of a streaming event, transforms it into text via AI, translates it into three languages, and reinserts it into the video feed as subtitles. 
Specifying that caching is applied after the initial function, the service begins with an audioExtractorVF allocated at the edge 
connected to a speechToTextVF located in the cloud and a multiTranslatorVF located in the cloud. Preferring that the total chain 
hardware is lower than 100 gb, and strictly requiring that the latency from the speechToTextVF to the final node remains 
below 20 ms, the system completes the pipeline with a subtitleInjectorVF allocated at the edge.

The enterprise provider corpDocOp requires a document classification engine to manage 50,000 daily files. This system analyzes PDF 
files or OCR scans, identifies the document type like invoice, contract, or reminder, and routes it to the competent business function. 
Specifying that security is applied after the initial phase, and mandating that this first component and the textExtractorVF are deployed on the same hosting node, the service begins with an ocrScannerVF allocated at the edge connected to a textExtractorVF 
located in the edge. Strictly requiring that the latency from the textExtractorVF to the aiDocumentClassifierVF remains below 50 ms, the 
chain incorporates an aiDocumentClassifierVF located in the cloud. Ensuring that privacy is executed before the dataRedactorVF, the chain connects 
to a dataRedactorVF located in the cloud. Finally, preferring a bandwidth higher than 500 mbps between the aiDocumentClassifierVF and the final 
distribution point, the system completes the pipeline with a documentRouterVF located in the cloud.

The financial provider fraudSafeOp requires an antifraud analysis service to manage 200,000 transactions per hour. This system intercepts every digital 
payment request, compares it with habitual user spending patterns via machine learning, and authorizes the transaction in a few milliseconds. 
Specifying that security is applied after the initial node, and mandating that the requestInterceptorVF and the profileMatcherVF are deployed 
on the same edge node, the service begins with a requestInterceptorVF allocated at the edge connected to a profileMatcherVF at the edge. Ensuring that privacy 
is executed before the mlAnalyzerVF, the chain incorporates an mlAnalyzerVF located in the cloud. Preferring that the bandwidth from the mlAnalyzerVF to 
the policyEnforcerVF remains higher than 1000 mbps, the chain adds a policyEnforcerVF located in the cloud. Finally, preferring that the total chain hardware 
remains lower than 120 gb, the system completes the pipeline with a responseEmitterVF located in the cloud.

The financial provider hftGlobalOp requires a high frequency trading service to manage 500,000 orders. This infrastructure receives stock prices, 
executes decision algorithms, and sends purchase orders seeking the fastest network path. Specifying that caching is applied after the initial function, the service begins with a marketFeedVF allocated at the edge. Mandating that the latency from this first component to the tradingAlgoVF remains 
below 50 ms, the chain connects to a tradingAlgoVF allocated at the edge. Preferring that the bandwidth from the tradingAlgoVF to the riskCheckerVF remains 
higher than 5000 mbps, the chain incorporates a riskCheckerVF located in the cloud. Preferring that the latency from the riskCheckerVF to the final node remains below 5 ms, and ensuring that logging is executed before this final component, the system completes the pipeline with an orderDispatcherVF allocated 
at the edge.

The financial provider onlineBankOp requires a digital identity verification service to manage 10,000 daily uploads. This service processes photos of 
documents uploaded by users, verifies their authenticity, and compares the data with international blacklists to prevent money laundering. Specifying that 
encoding is applied after the initial receiving function, the service begins with a documentReceiverVF allocated at the edge. Ensuring that security is 
executed before the second phase, the chain connects to an authenticityCheckerVF located in the cloud. Specifying that privacy is applied after the 
amlMatcherVF, the chain incorporates an amlMatcherVF located in the cloud. Finally, ensuring that compression is executed before the final 
node, the system completes the pipeline with a profileCreatorVF located in the cloud.

The service provider eInvoiceOp requires a digital invoicing service to manage 50,000 invoices per day. This system transforms sales data into certified XML files, 
applies the digital signature, and automatically sends them to governmental systems for fiscal validation. Mandating that the total chain hardware remains lower 
than 150 gb, the service begins with a saleDataCollectorVF allocated at the edge connected to an xmlConverterVF located in the cloud. Strictly requiring that the 
latency from the xmlConverterVF to the digitalSignerVF remains below 30 ms, the chain incorporates a digitalSignerVF located in the cloud. Finally, preferring 
that the bandwidth from the digitalSignerVF to the final point remains higher than 100 mbps, the system completes the pipeline with a taxAuthorityTransmitterVF located in the cloud.

The logistics provider deliveryLogisticsOp requires a route optimization service to manage 15,000 couriers. This software receives the GPS positions of a fleet, 
analyzes city traffic data, constantly recalculates the best route for each courier, and updates their terminals. Specifying that compression is applied after the 
initial node, the service begins with a gpsIngesterVF allocated at the edge connected to a trafficAnalyzerVF located in the cloud and a routeOptimizerVF 
located in the cloud. Ensuring that decoding is executed before the final node, the system incorporates a terminalUpdaterVF allocated at the edge. 
Finally, strictly requiring that the latency from the begin to the end of the chain remains below 80 ms, the system completes the optimization pipeline.

The municipal provider smartParkOp requires a parking management backend to handle 100,000 active parking spots. This system receives occupancy alerts, 
updates the city map, and processes automatic payments. Specifying that compression is applied after the initial function, the service begins with 
a sensorDataCollectorVF at the edge. Mandating the next two components are 
deployed on dedicated nodes, and ensuring encoding is applied before the paymentProcessorVF, the chain connected to a mapUpdaterVF in the cloud and a paymentProcessorVF in the cloud. Ensuring that logging is executed before the statusLoggerVF the chain continues to a statusLoggerVF 
in the cloud. The system includes a securityEnforcerVF in the cloud. Applying security after the paymentProcessorVF, and strictly requiring that the latency from the sensorDataCollectorVF to the final securityEnforcerVF remains below 30 ms, the system completes 
the pipeline.

The logistics provider aeroDeliveryOp requires a drone fleet control service to manage 5,000 active delivery drones. This system manages digital flight plans, 
avoids software collisions, and ensures that the command signal is always a priority. Specifying that caching is applied after the initial function, 
the service begins with a flightTelemetryIngesterVF ingester allocated at the edge. Mandating that the latency from this first component to the collisionAvoiderVF remains 
below 10 ms, the chain connects to a collisionAvoiderVF located in the cloud. Preferring that the total chain hardware remains lower than 200 gb, the chain 
incorporates a commandPrioritizerVF located in the cloud. Finally, preferring that the bandwidth from the collisionAvoiderVF to the final point remains 
higher than 2000 mbps, the system completes the pipeline with a routeDispatcherVF allocated at the edge.

The cybersecurity provider secureMailOp requires a service to manage 10,000 corporate mailboxes. This pipeline intercepts incoming emails, 
removes phishing links, analyzes attachments in an isolated environment, and delivers only safe messages to the server. Requiring decoding 
to be applied after the initial node, the chain begins with a mailGatewayVF allocated at the edge. Preferring a latency below 50 milliseconds, 
the mailGatewayVF connects to a phishingFilterVF located in the cloud. With a mandatory requirement for bandwidth higher than 100 Mbps, the filter 
links to a sandboxScannerVF located in the cloud. Applying strictly required logging before this node, the sandboxScannerVF is integrated into 
the chain. Finally, the service concludes by connecting the sandboxScannerVF to a safeDeliveryVF node located in the cloud.

The infrastructure provider serverMonOp requires a telemetry monitoring service to manage 50,000 virtual machines. This service collects temperature, 
CPU load, and memory usage data, aggregating them to identify anomalies before failure occurs. Specifying that it is mandatory for the telemetryCollectorVF and thedataAggregatorVF to be deployed on the same hosting node, the service begins with a telemetryCollectorVF at the edge connected 
to adataAggregatorVF at the edge. Strictly requiring that the latency from the begin to the end of the chain remains below 100 ms, and preferring 
that the bandwidth from the begin to the end of the chain remains higher than 2000 mbps, the chain incorporates an anomalyDetectorVF in the cloud. 
Finally, the system completes the pipeline with an alertDispatcherVF in the cloud.

The industrial provider autoWarehouseOp requires a remote control system for autonomous machines to manage 500 warehouse robots. 
This software receives sensor data, calculates paths to avoid collisions, and sends steering and braking commands. Specifying that decoding 
is applied after the initial node, the service begins with a sensorDataDecoderVF allocated at the edge connected to a collisionPathSolverVF located in the cloud. Strictly requiring that the latency from the sensorDataDecoderVF to commandEncoderVF remains below 500 ms, and ensuring that encoding is executed 
before the final instruction generator, the system completes the pipeline with a commandEncoderVF allocated at the edge.

The healthcare provider healthCareOp requires a post-operative tele-monitoring service to manage 5,000 active patients. 
This service receives digitalized patient vital data from home, analyzes cardiac anomalies, and notifies the doctor on duty immediately in case of danger. 
Specifying that privacy is applied after the initial unit, the service begins with a patientDataReceiverVF allocated at the edge connected to a 
cardiacAnomalyAnalyzerVF located in the cloud. Ensuring that logging is executed before, the chain incorporates a medicalAlertLoggerVF 
located in the cloud. Finally, strictly requiring that the latency from the patientDataReceiverVF to the final node remains below 100 ms, 
and preferring that the total chain hardware remains lower than 80 gb, the system completes the pipeline with a doctorNotifierVF located in the cloud.

The healthcare provider medDiagnosticOp requires a radiology AI diagnostics service to manage 10,000 daily scans. 
This pipeline receives high-resolution medical images, processes them with computer vision algorithms to highlight suspicious lesions, and stores them securely. 
Specifying that data compression is applied after the initial receiving function, the service begins with a dicomIngesterVF allocated at the edge. 
Preferring that the network bandwidth from this first component to thelesionAnalyzerVF remains higher than 500 mbps, the chain connects to a lesionAnalyzerVF located in the cloud. Mandating that thislesionAnalyzerVF and the subsequent metadataExtractorVF are strictly deployed on dedicated infrastructure servers, 
the chain incorporates both blocks at the cloud. Finally, ensuring encoding is executed before the final unit, the system completes the pipeline 
with a secureArchiverVF located in the cloud.

The digital provider secureVoteOp requires a certified electronic voting service to manage 200,000 voters. This platform for public or corporate consultations 
guarantees vote anonymity and prevents data manipulation. Preferring that the network bandwidth from the entry unit to the next phase remains higher than 
100 mbps, the service begins with a ballotIngesterVF allocated at the edge connected to an anonymizerVoteVF located in the cloud. Specifying that user privacy is 
applied after this anonymizerVoteVF process, and ensuring that security is executed before the integrityEnforcerVF, the chain incorporates an integrityEnforcerVF 
located in the cloud. The pipeline proceeds to a voteCounterVF located in the cloud. Finally, ensuring that logging is executed before the last
unit, the system completes the pipeline with an electoralAuditLoggerVF located in the cloud.

The digital provider govDataOp requires an open data portal service to manage 30,000 dataset downloads per day. This system extracts datasets from public databases, 
normalizes them into open formats, adds search metadata, and makes them available for public download. Strictly requiring that the response latency from the initial 
function to the final VNF below 200 ms, the service begins with a data extractor allocated at the edge. Specifying caching is 
applied after the formatNormalizerVF, the chain connects to a formatNormalizerVF located in the cloud. Mandating that this formatNormalizerVF and the 
subsequent metadataEnricherVF are hosted together on the exact same physical server, and preferring that the network bandwidth between them remains higher 
than 1000 mbps, the chain incorporates both blocks in cloud. Finally, the system completes the pipeline with a downloadProviderVF located in the cloud.

The educational provider eduCloudOp requires a virtual student lab platform to support 10,000 concurrent students. This system provides temporary programming 
environments, manages resource allocation for each student, and monitors the workspaces to prevent improper use. Preferring that the aggregate infrastructure 
footprint stays below 120 gb. Specifying privacy mechanisms are applied after the initial node, the service begins with a sessionIngesterVF 
allocated at the edge. Demanding that the network capacity from sessionIngesterVF to the resourceAllocatorVF more than 500 mbps, the chain connects 
to a resourceAllocatorVF located in the cloud. Ensuring that the latency from the sessionIngesterVF to the activityMonitorVF is kept under 40 ms, 
and that security are executed before the activityMonitorVF, the pipeline incorporates an activityMonitorVF located in the cloud. The system then flows 
through a userPrivacyEnforcerVF located in the cloud. Ensuring that logging are executed before the auditLoggerVF, the chain connects to an auditLoggerVF located in the cloud. Finally,  and ensuring compression is applied after the final function, the pipeline completes with anoutputPackagerVF 
located in the cloud.

The marketing provider sentimentOp requires a customer sentiment analysis platform to manage 100,000 daily reviews and comments. 
This software scans social media inputs, identifies prevailing emotions toward specific products, and sends weekly reports to the marketing department. 
Specifying that data privacy mechanisms are applied after the socialDataReceiverVF, the service begins with a socialDataReceiverVF allocated at the edge. 
Ensuring that security is executed before the next node, the chain connects to a sentimentAnalyzerVF located in the cloud. 
Mandating that this sentimentAnalyzerVF and the subsequent reportDispatcherVF are strictly deployed together on the same physical server node, 
the system completes the pipeline with a reportDispatcherVF located in the cloud.

The industrial provider factoryCloudOp requires an augmented reality back-end service to support 500 active smart glasses on the shop floor. 
This service sends visual technical instructions to workers' headsets, overlaying maintenance data on the framed machinery in real time. Strictly 
requiring that the total delivery latency from the initial arStreamReceiverVF to the arStreamDispatcherVF remains below 12 ms, the service begins 
with an arStreamReceiverVF allocated at the edge. Preferring that the network bandwidth from this point to the arPoseEstimatorVF remains higher 
than 200 mbps, the chain connects to an arPoseEstimatorVF located in the cloud. Mandating that this arPoseEstimatorVF and the subsequent tool 
are deployed on separate, dedicated infrastructure servers to guarantee isolated performance, the chain incorporates a dataOverlayEngineVF located in the cloud. 
Finally, preferring that the total chain hardware remains lower than 90 gb, the system completes the pipeline with an ar stream dispatcher located in the cloud.

The digital provider subscriptionOp requires a SaaS subscription management service to manage 50,000 active accounts. This recurring billing service handles 
customer payment cycles, software plan upgrades, and automated reminders for expired credit cards. Specifying that customer privacy is applied after the 
initial point, the service begins with a subscriptionIngesterVF allocated at the edge. Ensuring that decoding is executed before the billingCycleProcessorVF, the chain connects to a billingCycleProcessorVF located in the cloud. Mandating that transaction logging is executed before the dunningManagerVF, 
the pipeline incorporates a dunningManagerVF located in the cloud. Finally, ensuring encoding is executed before the invoiceGeneratorVF stage, the system 
completes the pipeline with an invoiceGeneratorVF located in the cloud.

The website security provider ddosProtectionOp requires an anti-DDoS defense system to handle 50,000 active web users. This system analyzes incoming traffic,
cleans malicious flows, and ensures server availability. Demanding a strictly required bandwidth greater than 500 megabps between them, the service begins
with a networkTrafficAnalyzerVF located at the edge linked to a scrubbingFilterVF located in the cloud. Mandating that security is processed before the scrubbingFilterVF, 
the chain then proceeds to a rateLimiterVF located in the cloud. Finally, specifying that logging should ideally be performed after the rateLimiterVF, and preferring 
a latency lower than 10 ms, the system connects to the final webServerVF located in the cloud.

The software provider devToolsOp requires a code efficiency analyzer service to manage 20,000 daily evaluation requests. This platform receives code snippets, 
executes a simulated runtime execution, and suggests specific optimizations to reduce computational resource consumption. Specifying that data caching is applied 
after the second function, the service begins with a codeReceiverVF allocated at the edge linked to a syntaxValidatorVF located in the cloud. The pipeline proceeds 
through a sandboxSimulatorVF located in the cloud and an optimizationEngineVF located in the cloud. Finally, preferring that the total chain hardware remains lower 
than 110 gb, and ensuring that data compression is applied after the final layer, the system completes the pipeline with a developersReportGeneratorVF located in 
the cloud.

The compliance provider gdprComplianceOp requires a GDPR verification service to manage 5,000 corporate database connections. This service scans corporate databases 
to identify unprotected personal data, applies automatic anonymization, and generates reports for regulators. Mandating that privacy is applied after the dbScannerVF, and preferring a latency lower than 20 ms between them, the service begins with a dbScannerVF allocated at the edge connected to an anonymizerVF 
located in the cloud. Specifying a strictly required bandwidth higher than 50 Mbps before moving to the next component, the chain incorporates a reportGeneratorVF 
located in the cloud. Finally, enforcing that security must be executed before the reportGeneratorVF, the system completes the compliance pipeline.

The network security provider secureCryptoOp requires an encrypted traffic analysis service to support 25,000 corporate users. This service inspects HTTPS flows 
without fully decrypting them, using AI to identify malware or botnet patterns. Specifying that decoding is applied after the first VNF, and mandating that 
this initial component and the subsequent featureExtractorVF service are deployed on the same hosting node, the service begins with a trafficSplitterVF allocated at 
the edge connected to a featureExtractorVF located in the edge. Preferring that the total chain hardware is lower than 80 gigabytes, the chain incorporates 
an aiClassifierVF located in the cloud followed by an alertManagerVF located in the cloud. Finally, ensuring that security is executed before the final policyEnforcerVF point, 
the system completes the pipeline with a policyEnforcerVF located in the cloud.

The government provider govMessagingOp requires a service to manage 50,000 institutional messages. This service receives digital communications, 
verifies the electronic signature of the sender, checks its integrity, and archives the message in a legal vault. Specifying that caching is 
applied after the first function, the service begins with a msgReceiverVF allocated at the edge. Mandating that the sigVerifierVF and the integrityCheckerVF are deployed on the same hosting node, the chain connects to a sigVerifierVF located in the cloud and 
an integrityCheckerVF located in the cloud. Preferring that the total chain hardware is lower than 100 gb, and ensuring that compression is 
executed before the final legalVaultVF, the system completes the pipeline with a legalVaultVF located in the cloud.

Cloud gaming service provider GamingOp needs a service to handle 40,000 active players. This service runs games on powerful servers and 
delivers the video stream to the user, ensuring very low latency to prevent the game from becoming unplayable. Specifying that encoding 
be applied after the initial gameExecutorVF, the service begins with a gameExecutorVF hosted in the cloud. Preferring that this first component 
operate on a dedicated node, the chain includes a streamPackerVF hosted in the cloud. Finally, strictly requiring that the latency from 
the streamPackerVF to the final deliveryOptimizerVF remain less than 30 ms and that it operates on a dedicated node, the system 
completes the pipeline with a deliveryOptimizerVF hosted at the edge.

The media provider mediaBroadcastOp requires a live multicamera streaming service to support 30,000 concurrent viewers. 
This system receives video streams from different angles, allows cloud mixing, adds advertising graphics, and distributes the signal to 
thousands of viewers simultaneously. Specifying that compression is applied after the initial streamIngesterVF, the service begins with a 
streamIngesterVF allocated at the edge connected to a cloudStudioVF located in the cloud. Mandating a bandwidth higher than 5000 mbps between 
the upcoming graphicInjectorVF and the final destination, the chain incorporates a graphicInjectorVF located in the cloud. 
Preferring that the total chain hardware is lower than 150 gb, and ensuring that caching is executed before the final streamDistributorVF, 
the system completes the pipeline with a streamDistributorVF located in the cloud.

Media provider vodStreamOp needs a video-on-demand distribution service to handle 80,000 active subscribers. 
This service optimizes movie distribution by encrypting content with DRM, compressing it into various formats, and storing it on nodes close 
to the user to avoid buffering. By specifying that encoding be applied after the initial drmEncryptorVF and preferring that this first 
component and the subsequent transcoderVF service be deployed on the same hosting node, the service begins with a drmEncryptorVF hosted in the 
cloud and connected to a transcoderVF also hosted in the cloud. Requiring bandwidth exceeding 10,000 Mbps before moving on to the next element, 
the chain includes a cachingNodeVF node hosted at the edge. Finally, by ensuring that decoding is performed before the cachingNodeVF at the edge, 
the system completes the video-on-demand distribution pipeline.
